author: security-reviewer

findings.description: Class sweep for the same untrusted-page-parameter pattern found one further instance outside this change set: VetController.showVetList still passes an unclamped @RequestParam page into PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize), so /vets.html?page=0 reaches the error page exactly as /owners?page=0 did before this fix. It is pre-existing and out of REQ-OWN-002's owner-scoped surface, so it is not a finding against this change; flagging it so a follow-up slice can be decided rather than lost.

recommendations: Non-numeric input (/owners?page=abc) still fails binding and renders the error page. That path is unchanged by this fix and is not a disclosure risk here: templates/error.html renders ${message} through th:text, which Thymeleaf escapes, so no request-derived markup reaches the DOM.
If the vets listing gets the same clamp later, extracting the shared FIRST_PAGE constant and the clamp into one place would keep the two controllers from drifting.
approved_aspects: Clamp is applied at the trust boundary, in the controller method that receives the query-string value, before it reaches any collaborator — matching security-principles.md's rule that defensive checks belong at the boundary rather than scattered through the core.

Math.max(requestedPage, FIRST_PAGE) is total over the int domain: no negative index can reach PageRequest.of, and because the clamped value is at least 1, the page - FIRST_PAGE subtraction cannot underflow. The upper bound needs no clamp — Integer.MAX_VALUE yields offset (long) pageNumber * pageSize in Spring Data's AbstractPageRequest, so no overflow, and the repository simply returns an empty page.
No change to the data-access path: the query remains the Spring Data derived findByLastNameStartingWith with a Pageable, so no string-concatenated query text and no new injection surface.
Rendered model attributes are unchanged in kind; currentPage is an int and reaches the template through Thymeleaf's default-escaping expression output.
No new endpoint, no widening of the exposed surface, no new request-bound field, and no change to any data binder's disallowed-field list.
No credential, token, key, or other secret-shaped literal anywhere in the diff; the only new constant is the integer FIRST_PAGE.

Supply chain unaffected: the change set is two Java files, with no edit to build.gradle, the plugin block, or any dependency coordinate or repository declaration, so no new artifact is resolved and no version moves.

Net effect on the threat model is a reduction: one request-triggered path to the error page (which renders the underlying exception message) is removed, so the change leaves the application no weaker than the baseline in system-design.md's Security Context.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: The javadoc on `findPaginatedForOwnersLastName` opens straight into `@param` with no summary sentence describing what the method does; Javadoc convention (and the rest of this file's public/method docs, e.g. `showOwner`) puts a one-line description first, then the tags. As written, a generated-docs reader sees a blank summary for this method.
findings.fix: Add a one-sentence summary before the `@param` tag, e.g. "Looks up one page of owners matching the given last name."

findings.description: Confirmed: VetController.findPaginated (line 61) constructs `PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize)` from an unclamped `@RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page` (line 45) with no lower-bound check — the identical defect this slice fixes for /owners, reachable via `/vets.html?page=0` or lower. Leaving it out of REQ-OWN-002 is the right scope call: it's a different controller/bounded context (vet package, not owner) and the PRD requirement this slice implements (`[REQ-OWN-002]`) only covers owner search, so fixing VetController here would be undocumented scope creep. But the twin bug is now a known, unrecorded defect with no PRD line to track it. Recommend opening a companion requirement/backlog item for the vets listing before this is forgotten.

approved_aspects: FIRST_PAGE constant and Math.max clamp read clearly and are documented with a why-comment explaining the clamp happens because query-string input is untrusted
Parameter rename from `page` to `requestedPage` for the raw @RequestParam avoids shadowing the clamped `page` used everywhere else in the method — clear and unambiguous
Javadoc on findPaginatedForOwnersLastName correctly documents the precondition that callers must clamp before calling, and why (PageRequest rejects negative index)

New test processFindFormWithPageBelowOneReturnsFirstPage exercises both a zero and negative page value, asserts the model's currentPage attribute, and independently verifies the repository received page index 0 via ArgumentCaptor — matches the existing loop-driven verification pattern already used by processFindFormIgnoresSurroundingWhitespace in this file
checkFormat passes clean on both changed files

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The test iterates over page values 0 and -5 with a `for` loop in the test body. testing-principles.md § Assertions bars branching/loops in test bodies ('No branching in assertions... loops. Use collection-aware assertions instead') and the Agent Decision Checklist item 4 ('Linearity: No branching or loops in the test body'). Convert to a `@ParameterizedTest` with `@CsvSource` over the two clamp inputs (0 and -5), asserting status/view/currentPage per invocation, the way a table-driven test should read.
findings.fix: Replace the `for (String pageBelowFirst : List.of("0", "-5"))` loop with `@ParameterizedTest` + `@ValueSource(strings = {"0", "-5"})` (or `@CsvSource`) taking the page parameter, keeping the ArgumentCaptor assertion on `getPageNumber()` per invocation or moved to a second focused test.

findings.description: testing-principles.md § Test Naming mandates the BDD school `the{Subject}Should{Outcome}` for tests written from 2026-07-31 onward, and explicitly calls out naming a test after the controller method under test (its own bad example is `processFindFormByLastName`) as an implementation name, not a behavior name. This brand-new test is named `processFindFormWithPageBelowOneReturnsFirstPage`, repeating exactly that anti-pattern.

approved_aspects: The clamp is genuinely pinned: page=0 and page=-5 both drive PageRequest.of(page-1,...) which throws IllegalArgumentException pre-fix, so the test fails on a regression, not just on the happy path.
Both the model attribute (currentPage=1) and the actual zero-based Pageable passed to the repository are asserted, covering the fix at both the view layer and the persistence-call layer.
AssertJ used for the Pageable assertion (assertThat(...).extracting(...).containsOnly(0)).

author: doc-reviewer

findings.description: REQ-OWN-002's paged-listing behavior now has a specific, tested contract for an out-of-range page request (a page number below the first page is clamped to page 1, per OwnerController.java:100-102 and the new OwnerControllerTests.processFindFormWithPageBelowOneReturnsFirstPage test), but the PRD states nothing about it. The existing edge-case list already covers a sibling boundary case for REQ-OWN-002 (item 1, blank-search normalization) at the same altitude, so a reader of docs/prd.md alone cannot learn this behavior is intentional rather than the bug it used to be. Add a numbered edge case under REQ-OWN-002's 'Edge cases' list stating, in behavioral terms, that a requested page below the first page returns the first page rather than an error.

The new Javadoc on findPaginatedForOwnersLastName opens directly with @param, omitting the one-line method summary every other multi-line Javadoc block in this file carries (see the showOwner Javadoc at line 176: 'Custom handler for displaying an owner.'). This deviates from the file's own Javadoc convention.
findings.fix:
Add a summary line before @param, e.g.: /**
 * Finds one page of owners whose last name starts with the given prefix.
 * @param page the requested page, counting from {@link #FIRST_PAGE}; callers clamp it
 * before calling, because {@link PageRequest} rejects a negative index
 */

approved_aspects: FIRST_PAGE constant is named and documented instead of a bare magic number
The clamp-before-use comment on processFindForm accurately explains why the clamp happens where it does
Cross-references between the Javadoc and the code (FIRST_PAGE, PageRequest) resolve correctly
